phrases.syllabary_text: ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ ᏥᎷᎩ ᏌᎾᎴ ᎦᏳᎳᏅ ᏌᏊ ᎢᏳᏩᎦᏗ ᏱᏣᎶᏌ ᏙᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: khali'elika tsi'luki sanale kayulanv sakwu iyuwakati yitsalohs tohv
phrases.phonetic_broad: kalielika tsiluki sanale kayulanv sakwu iyuwakati yitsalos tov
phrases.english_text: I’m thankful for you coming here this morning. Already one time you have been through this, haven’t you?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: Yes.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏏᏭᏛ ᏴᎬᏯᏅᏓᏗᏍᏓ ᏄᏰᎵᏛ ᏥᏂᏓᏛᏁᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: siwutv yvkvyanvtatihst nuyelhit tsinittvneha
phrases.phonetic_broad: siwutv yvkvyanvtatist nuyelit tsinittvnea
phrases.english_text: Again, I’ll remind you the purpose of what we’re doing.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: vhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: Aha.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎯᎢᎾ ᏥᏓᎾᏕᎶᏆᎠ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎯᎠ ᏗᏜ ᏃᏭ ᏧᎾᏔᎾ ᏍᎩᏅ Ꮲ ᏱᏛᎾᎴᏅᎯ ᎠᎾᏛᏓᏍᏗᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ
phrases.phonetic_text: hi'ina tsitanatelohkwa'a tiniyoli hi'a titla nwu tsunathana skinv lhv yitvnlenvhi anthvtahstihv ohst tsalak kawonihihsti khsv

phrases.english_text: Those that are learning, the children this way, the adults that way, someday they’ll start listening to it, good Cherokee speaking.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏐᎢᎴ ᎨᏒ Ꮭ ᏳᏓᎷᎳ ᏗᎨᏣᎵᏏ ᏕᏣᎧᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: so'ile kehsv lha yutalula tiketsalihs tetsakhahv
phrases.phonetic_broad: soile kesv la yutalula tiketsalis tetsakav

phrases.phonetic_text: tskwhihsti'e
phrases.phonetic_broad: tskwistie
phrases.english_text: Yes, a lot of them!

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎯᎠᏛ ᎢᏧᎳᎮᏃ Ꮲ ᏱᏓᏂᎶᏐᏂ ᏍᎩᏅ ᏗᎨᏣᎵᏏ ᏳᎾᏚᎵ ᏢᏴ ᎤᎾᏛᎪᏗ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: hi'atv itsulheno tlhv yitanilohsoni skin tiketsalihs yuntuli lvyv unthvkoti hiwonihskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: iatv itsuleno tlv yitanilosoni skin tiketsalis yuntuli lvyv untvkoti iwoniskv
phrases.english_text: Both of us, someday we’ll pass on. Then your grandkids might want to hear you talking.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᏅ ᏳᎾᏓᏙᎮᎳ ᏳᏂᎷᏣ ᏱᎨᎦᎵᏍᎪᎸᏓᏏ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᏧᎾᏛᎪᏗ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎬᎢ
phrases.phonetic_text: skhinv yunatatohela yuniluhths yikekalihskolvhtahs kehehst tsunathvkot hiwonihskv'i
phrases.phonetic_broad: skinv yunatatoela yuniluts yikekaliskolvtas keest tsunatvkot iwoniskvi
phrases.english_text: If they ask and come here, they will let them listen to it.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏯᎾᏛᏓᏍᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: yantthsta
phrases.phonetic_broad: yanttsta
phrases.english_text: There they can listen to it.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv vv
phrases.english_text: Yes, yes.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᎬᏱ ᎨᎲ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎧᎵ ᏕᏣᏙᎥ ᏍᎩᏃᎯᏌ
phrases.phonetic_text: akvyi kehv yonek khali tetsato'v skhinohihsa
phrases.phonetic_broad: akvyi kev yonek kali tetsatov skinoisa
phrases.english_text: First thing, tell me your full English name.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᎳᎩᎾ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsalakna
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsalakna
phrases.english_text: And in Cherokee?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎺᎵ ᎹᎦᏱ
phrases.phonetic_text: meli makayi
phrases.phonetic_broad: meli makayi
phrases.english_text: Me-li Ma-Ga-Yi.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎹᎦᏱ
phrases.phonetic_text: makayi
phrases.phonetic_broad: makayi
phrases.english_text: Ma-Ga-Yi…

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᏣᎵ Shell ᏓᏩᏙᎠ
phrases.phonetic_text: ayatv tsali hsaw tawato'a
phrases.phonetic_broad: ayatv tsali saw tawatoa
phrases.english_text: For me, Charlie Shell is my name.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᎳᎩᏃ ᎬᏗ ᏩᎴᎵ ᏓᏩᏙᎠ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsalakino kvti waleli tawa'to'a
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsalakino kvti waleli tawatoa
phrases.english_text: In Cherokee it is Wa-Le-Li (Hummingbird)

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏩᎴᎵ ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: wallhi v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: walli vv
phrases.english_text: Wa-Le-Li.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᏢ ᏣᏕᏁ
phrases.phonetic_text: halhv tsatenhe
phrases.phonetic_broad: alv tsatene
phrases.english_text: Where were you born?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏩᏕᏅᎩ ᏗᏓᏁᎸᏭᎮᏃ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ᎡᎵ ᏍᏓᏱ
phrases.phonetic_text: awatenhvhki titanelvwheno awatenhv el stayi
phrases.phonetic_broad: awatenvki titanelvweno awatenv el stayi
phrases.english_text: I was born at home. It was pretty hard.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᎦᏓᏅᏒᎮᏃ ᎥᎿ ᏗᏩᏕᏅ ᎾᎮᏃ Caney ᎢᎯᏲ ᎤᏪᏴ ᎾᎥ ᏣᏃᏎᎲ ᏪᎵᏂ ᏗᏜ ᏚᏭᎪᏛ
phrases.phonetic_text: okata'nvhshenho vnha tiwten nhen kheni ihiyo uweyv na'v tsanohsehv welini tila tuwukohtv
phrases.phonetic_broad: okatanvseno vna tiwten nen keni iiyo uweyv nav tsanosev welini tila tuwukotv
phrases.english_text: We have moved from where I was born there at Caney, near Caney Creek, they called it, towards Welling.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: Yes.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: Yes.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᏢ ᎨᎲ Ꮩ ᏣᏛᏏᏙᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: halhv kehv to tsathvhsitolv
phrases.phonetic_broad: alv kev to tsatvsitolv
phrases.english_text: Where for sure you grew up at, there? Where you’re talking about?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎿᎨ ᏥᏃᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: vnhake tshinohe
phrases.phonetic_broad: vnake tsinoe
phrases.english_text: Where for sure you grew up at, there? Where you’re talking about?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎯᏍᎩ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ᎥᎿ ᏬᎦᏓᏅᏌᏃ ᏃᏭ ᎦᏚᏏ Babo ᎠᏃᏎᎲ ᏃᏭᏃ ᏩᏩᏛᏒ
phrases.phonetic_text: hihski tsutethiyvta awatenv vnha wokatanvhsan nowu katuhs tato anhsehv nowunho wawathvhsv
phrases.phonetic_broad: iski tsutetiyvta awatenv vna wokatanvsan nowu katus tato ansev nowuno wawatvsv
phrases.english_text: Five years I lived there. We moved then to the top of the mountain, “Ba-Bo” they called it, where I grew up at.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᏍ Sam MccoyᎢᏍ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏨᏂ ᎨᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: nahs hsam makho'ihs kohuhst tsvni kehe
phrases.phonetic_broad: nas sam makois koust tsvni kee
phrases.english_text: Sam McCoy, was he your cousin?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᎶᏏᏅ ᎦᏳᎳᏅ ᏍᏈᏍᏗ ᏚᎾᏛᎦᎾ Ꮭ ᏱᎩᎾᏝᏃᎮᏞ Guy ᎠᏎ ᏍᏓᏝᏃᎮᏞ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsalohsnv kayulnv skwihst tunathvkana la yikinalhanohelhe ka ahs stalhanohelhe
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsalosnv kayulnv skwist tunatvkana la yikinalanoele ka as stalanoele
phrases.english_text: Brother-in-law… You’ve been through this before already, a lot of them have heard it. It wasn’t me that you talked to, it was probably Guy.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏏᏭᏅ ᏛᎦᏁᎸᏔᏂ ᏍᏗ ᎩᏂᏃᎮᏗ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏗᏣᎶᏒ ᎨᏒ ᏂᎯ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ ᎥᎾ
phrases.phonetic_text: siwun tvkanelhvhthanhi sti kininohehti nuhst titsalohsv kehsv nihi skina skinohihsi vna
phrases.phonetic_broad: siwun tvkanelvtani sti kininoeti nust titsalosv kesv nii skina skinoisi vna
phrases.english_text: But I will try again. We have to talk a little about where you came from. Tell me about when you were a kid, what was it like where you all came from, what you all played, or everything you all did. Tell me about that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎯ ᎯᏲᏟ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏗᏥᎶᏒ ᏕᏣᏁᎶᏂᏙᎸ ᏂᎦᏓᎴ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏂᏣᏛᏁᎯ ᏍᎩᎾᎭ ᏥᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ
phrases.phonetic_text: nihi hiyolhi tsikehv nuhstv titsilohsv tetsanelonhitolv nikatle kohuhsti nitsatvnehi skinaha tsihskinohihsi
phrases.phonetic_broad: nii iyoli tsikev nustv titsilosv tetsanelonitolv nikatle kousti nitsatvnei skinaa tsiskinoisi
phrases.english_text: But I will try again. We have to talk a little about where you came from. Tell me about when you were a kid, what was it like where you all came from, what you all played, or everything you all did. Tell me about that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎿᎮᏃ babo ᎠᎩᎷᏨᎢ Eight
phrases.phonetic_text: vnhheno tato aki'luhtsv'i et
phrases.phonetic_broad: vneno tato akilutsvi et
phrases.english_text: I came to Barber when I was 18 months old. Mom and Dad had divorced. We came to Barber, and Dad was living in Vian. My brother is older than me. He also grew up in Vian. I grew up in Barber. When us kids were playing around, there was mostly Cherokee kids that lived there, when we were playing.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᏁᎳᏚ ᎢᏯᏅᏓ ᎦᎨᎥ ᎠᎩᎷᏨᎢ ᎡᏥᎮᏃ ᎡᏙᏓᏃ ᏚᎾᎦᎴᏅᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: na nelatu iyanvt kake'v akiluhtsv'i etsiheno etotano tunakalenvha
phrases.phonetic_broad: na nelatu iyanvt kakev akilutsvi etsieno etotano tunakalenva
phrases.english_text: I came to Barber when I was 18 months old. Mom and Dad had divorced. We came to Barber, and Dad was living in Vian. My brother is older than me. He also grew up in Vian. I grew up in Barber. When us kids were playing around, there was mostly Cherokee kids that lived there, when we were playing.

phrases.syllabary_text: Babo ᎣᎩᏂᎷᏨᎢ ᏃᏭᏃ Vian ᏓᏰᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎥᎩᏙᏃ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᏴ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎿ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏛᏒ Vian ᏗᏜ
phrases.phonetic_text: tato okiniluhtsv'i nowuno tian ta'yhv etota vkitono akayliyv aya khv vnh skwu uthsv tian titla
phrases.phonetic_broad: tato okinilutsvi nowuno tian tayv etota vkitono akayliyv aya kv vn skwu utsv tian titla
phrases.english_text: I came to Barber when I was 18 months old. Mom and Dad had divorced. We came to Barber, and Dad was living in Vian. My brother is older than me. He also grew up in Vian. I grew up in Barber. When us kids were playing around, there was mostly Cherokee kids that lived there, when we were playing.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏃᏭᏅ ᎥᎿᏭ ᏃᏭ Babo ᏗᏜ ᏩᏩᏛᏏᏙᎸ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏙᏣᏁᎶᏂᏙᎲ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎤᏟ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏁᎲ ᎥᎿ ᏙᏣᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬᎢ
phrases.phonetic_text: nowunv vnhawu nw tato ttla wwathvhsitolv nowunhv totsanelonhitohv tiniyoli tskwihsti anitsalak tiniyolhi utli ika anehv vnha totsanelohvhskv'i
phrases.phonetic_broad: nowunv vnawu nw tato ttla wwatvsitolv nowunv totsanelonitov tiniyoli tskwisti anitsalak tiniyoli utli ika anev vna totsanelovskvi
phrases.english_text: I came to Barber when I was 18 months old. Mom and Dad had divorced. We came to Barber, and Dad was living in Vian. My brother is older than me. He also grew up in Vian. I grew up in Barber. When us kids were playing around, there was mostly Cherokee kids that lived there, when we were playing.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᎳ ᏂᏥᎡ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: hala nitsi'e sitanelv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ala nitsie sitanelv

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏦᎢᏛ ᏃᏥ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎠᏱᏃ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸᎢᏃ ᏐᎢ
phrases.phonetic_text: tso'itv notsi vkito ayino tsohstatalv'ino s'i
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsoitv notsi vkito ayino tsostatalvino si
phrases.english_text: There are three of us, my brother, me, and my sister.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎦᏓᎲ Ꮟ ᎢᏤᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: nikathv si itseha
phrases.phonetic_broad: nikatv si itsea
phrases.english_text: Are all of you still living?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᏤᎭ ᏦᎩᎦᏴᎵᎨᏃ Ᏺ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎤᎾᏂᎩᏌ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v nikata otseha tsokikayvlikeno yo kayula unnhikihsa
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv nikata otsea tsokikayvlikeno yo kayula unnikisa
phrases.english_text: Yes, all of us are still alive. Our parents are already gone.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᎳ ᎢᎩᏓ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎢᏤᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: hala ikhita khalhitsote itsehe
phrases.phonetic_broad: ala ikita kalitsote itsee
phrases.english_text: How big was the house you all lived in?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᏤᎲ ᎥᎿ Ꮎ ᎢᎯᏲ ᏄᏪᏴ ᎾᎥ ᏦᏤᎲ ᏔᎵ
phrases.phonetic_text: otsehv vnha na ihiyo nuweyv n'v tsotsehv thali
phrases.phonetic_broad: otsev vna na iiyo nuweyv nv tsotsev tali
phrases.english_text: We lived near where Caney Creek was. We lived in a four-bedroom house there. There were fireplaces on both sides. When we were chased off, they took and moved half of the house. Then they brought it to the hill in Barber. And then, when they built onto the end of it, it became six bedrooms.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏅᎩᏛ ᏕᎧᏅᏑᎸ ᎣᏤᎲ ᎥᎿ ᏗᎪᏘᏗ ᏗᎪᏢᎯ ᎢᏧᎳ ᏗᎬᎩᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: nvhkitv tekhanvhsulv otsehv vnha tikothti tikolhvhi itsul tikvkiti
phrases.phonetic_broad: nvkitv tekanvsulv otsev vna tikotti tikolvi itsul tikvkiti
phrases.english_text: We lived near where Caney Creek was. We lived in a four-bedroom house there. There were fireplaces on both sides. When we were chased off, they took and moved half of the house. Then they brought it to the hill in Barber. And then, when they built onto the end of it, it became six bedrooms.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᏍᎩᏃ ᎣᎩᎨᎯᏙᎳ ᏃᏭ ᎠᏰᏟᏭ ᎢᎦ ᎤᏂᏫᏛᎲ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎤᏂᎲᏒ ᏃᏭ Babo ᎦᏚᏏ ᏭᏂᏲᏢ
phrases.phonetic_text: vhskino okikhehitol nowu ayelhiwu ika uniwhitvhv kalhitsote unihvhsv now tato katuhs wuniyholhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vskino okikeitol nowu ayeliwu ika uniwitvv kalitsote univsv now tato katus wuniyolv
phrases.english_text: We lived near where Caney Creek was. We lived in a four-bedroom house there. There were fireplaces on both sides. When we were chased off, they took and moved half of the house. Then they brought it to the hill in Barber. And then, when they built onto the end of it, it became six bedrooms.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎿ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏚᎾᏁᏍᎨᎲ ᎠᏍᏛ ᏗᏜ ᏚᏂᏁᏉᎥ ᏃᏭ ᏑᏓᎵ ᏗᎧᏅᏑᎸ ᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ ᏃᏭ
phrases.phonetic_text: vnha nowule tunnhehskehv ahstv tila tuninhekwo'v nowu sutal tikhanvhsulv nulhsthanv nowu
phrases.phonetic_broad: vna nowule tunneskev astv tila tuninekwov nowu sutal tikanvsulv nulstanv nowu
phrases.english_text: We lived near where Caney Creek was. We lived in a four-bedroom house there. There were fireplaces on both sides. When we were chased off, they took and moved half of the house. Then they brought it to the hill in Barber. And then, when they built onto the end of it, it became six bedrooms.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᏔᎾᎲ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ
phrases.phonetic_text: uthanhv kalitsote
phrases.phonetic_broad: utanv kalitsote
phrases.english_text: It was a big house, huh?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎦᎸᎳᏗᏃ ᎪᏢᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: khalvla'tino kolhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: kalvlatino kolv
phrases.english_text: It was tall too.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮩ ᎤᏰᏟᏕ ᎣᎩᎨᎯᏙᎳ ᏣᏗᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: to uyelhite okikhehitola tstha
phrases.phonetic_broad: to uyelite okikeitola tsta
phrases.english_text: What was the reason you say, “When we were chased off”?

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ ᎾᏃ ᎠᎹᏱ
phrases.phonetic_text: o nano amayi
phrases.phonetic_broad: o nano amayi
phrases.english_text: Oh, the creek!

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ ᏗᏂᏍᏚᏂᏎᏕ
phrases.phonetic_text: o tinihstunihsete

phrases.english_text: She never said what the reason was?

phrases.phonetic_text: hv'v skikwu ik tsinikawehv skinv ohsi nikehvna kehv wak hawiy yvki'a
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv skikwu ik tsinikawev skinv osi nikevna kev wak awiy yvkia
phrases.english_text: No, that's all that she said. Because it isn’t good if you eat meat.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏏᏆᎾ ᏥᏔᎩᏅ ᏕᏥᎾᏝᎡᏍ
phrases.phonetic_text: sihkwana tsithakinv tetsinalha'ehs
phrases.phonetic_broad: sikwana tsitakinv tetsinalaes
phrases.english_text: Did you have pigs and chickens?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᏥᏚᎾᏝᎥᏗ ᏍᏊ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v tsitunalha'vt skwu
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv tsitunalavt skwu
phrases.english_text: Yes, she had them too.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮭ Ᏺ ᏱᏕᏥᎯᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: tla y yittsihihe
phrases.phonetic_broad: tla y yittsiie
phrases.english_text: You didn’t kill them?

phrases.syllabary_text: Mhm ᏥᏔᎦ ᎤᏲᎢᏃ ᏄᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎮ ᏓᏂᏍᏓᏲᎯᎲ ᏳᏟᎢᎶᏝ
phrases.phonetic_text: amham tsithaka uyo'in nunalhstanhe tanihstyohihv yutli'ilola
phrases.phonetic_broad: amam tsitaka uyoin nunalstane tanistyoiv yutliilola
phrases.english_text: Mhm, the chickens. They had it bad when Christmas came.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏩᎦᏲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᎾᏛᏁ ᏙᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: wakayo ohst nnatvnhe tohv
phrases.phonetic_broad: wakayo ost nnatvne tov
phrases.english_text: The cows had it good though?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᎾᏛᏅ ᏌᏌ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏚᏂᎾᏝᎥ ᎾᏅ ᏗᏈᏍᏙ ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᎡᏥ Ꮎ ᎤᏄᏱᏔᏅ ᎦᏤᏍᏙ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏙᎩᎾᎥ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: ohsta nunatvhnv sahs skwu tsituninalha'v nn tikwhihsto tsitekolhskv etsi na unuyithanv katsehsto skwu tsitokina'v skyuhsti
phrases.phonetic_broad: osta nunatvnv sas skwu tsituninalav nn tikwisto tsitekolskv etsi na unuyitanv katsesto skwu tsitokinav skyusti
phrases.english_text: They had it good. We also had geese. Mama would make pillows with the feathers, and mattresses too.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᎮᏃ ᎦᏌᎴᎾ ᏏᏛᎮ ᏴᏩᏔ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ Ꮎ goose down ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎪᏢᏔᏅ ᏧᎦᎾᏫ ᎥᏍᎩ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: skheno kahsalena sitvhe yvwatha khitsiki na kuhs tan shki yuhst tikolthanv tsukanawi vhski iyuhsti
phrases.phonetic_broad: skeno kasalena sitve yvwata kitsiki na kus tan ski yust tikoltanv tsukanawi vski iyusti
phrases.english_text: Jackets today, you can still find them made with goose down. Those that are made like that are really warm.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎢᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᎮᎨ ᏗᎬᏄ
phrases.phonetic_text: itsalihsteliheke tikvnu
phrases.phonetic_broad: itsalistelieke tikvnu
phrases.english_text: Did you all help with… how do you say…

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᎨ ᏴᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: tokhe yta
phrases.phonetic_broad: toke yta
phrases.english_text: Did you all help with… how do you say…

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏗᎬᏄᏯᎩᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: tikvnuyakita
phrases.phonetic_broad: tikvnuyakita
phrases.english_text: Plucking their feathers.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᏦᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᎡᎵᏏᎮᏃ ᏗᎯᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᏭᏃ Ꭰ ᏥᏂᏕᎬᏁᎲ ᏥᏓᏍᏆᏄᏖᏲ ᏥᏓᎯᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v tsotslihstelihv elihsiheno tihihi tsikehv nawno a tsinitekvnehv tsitahskwanutheyo tstahihv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv tsotslisteliv elisieno tiii tsikev nawno a tsinitekvnev tsitaskwanuteyo tstaiv
phrases.english_text: We helped. Grandma used to kill them and then she went like this [gestures] when she twisted their necks when she killed them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᏔᎦᏛ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏗᎮ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsithakatv utloyi the tsikehv tohv
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsitakatv utloyi te tsikev tov
phrases.english_text: Kill chickens the same way back then, ain’t it? Did you all have a good garden back then?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏲᎨ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏓᏥᏫᏒᏗ ᏄᏍᏕ ᏍᎩ ᏲᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: yokhe ohsta ttsiwhsvt nuhste sk yonhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: yoke osta ttsiwsvt nuste sk yonv
phrases.english_text: Kill chickens the same way back then, ain’t it? Did you all have a good garden back then?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᎥᎿᏅ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏃᏭ ᎦᏚᏏ ᏍᏊ ᏧᏬᎩᎷᏨ ᎡᎵ ᎣᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎣᎬᏌ ᎣᎩᏍᏚᏟᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ ᎠᎹ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v vnhanv elati nowu katuhs skwu tsuwokiluhtsv eli ohsi tsikehv ahseno okvhsa okihstutlhst tskehv nowu ama
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv vnanv elati nowu katus skwu tsuwokilutsv eli osi tsikev aseno okvsa okistutlst tskev nowu ama
phrases.english_text: Yes, below. When we got to the mountain it was good, but we had to water it ourselves.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏛ
phrases.phonetic_text: totv
phrases.phonetic_broad: totv
phrases.english_text: You did?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎲ ᎥᎿ ᎨᏓᎵ ᎨᎲ Ᏺ Ꮎ ᏓᏓᏑᎶᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎯᏌᏛᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: vhv vnha khetli kehv yo na tatahsulohskv ohst tshinkalhsthv na amayulithi kehv ahihsathvhskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv vna ketli kev yo na tatasuloskv ost tsinkalstv na amayuliti kev aisatvskv
phrases.english_text: Uh-huh, down the hill it would give off dew. By the creek it did really good with the morning dew.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮩ ᎢᏨᏁᎮ ᎢᏥᏓᎷᎩᏍᎨ
phrases.phonetic_text: to itsvnhe itsitalukihske
phrases.phonetic_broad: to itsvne itsitalukiske
phrases.english_text: How did y’all plow the ground?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏐᏈᎵ ᏥᏓᏅᏗᎲ ᎦᏓᎷᎪᏗ ᏗᏂᎴᏅᎯᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: sokwili tstanhvhtihv katlukoti tinilenvhita
phrases.phonetic_broad: sokwili tstanvtiv katlukoti tinilenvita
phrases.english_text: They used a horse-drawn plow, and donkeys.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏕᏥᎾᏝᎡᎨ ᎩᎶᎨ ᏄᏓᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: tetsinalha'ek khiloke nutale
phrases.phonetic_broad: tetsinalaek kiloke nutale
phrases.english_text: Did you own them or did someone else?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏙ ᏥᏚᎾᏝᎥ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᎥ ᏥᏂᏚᎾᏓᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: elihs tsikehv ut tsitunalha'v vhskin na'v tsintunatalv
phrases.phonetic_broad: elis tsikev ut tsitunalav vskin nav tsintunatalv
phrases.english_text: Grandma’s brother owned them. They were neighbors.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮩ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏣᏛᏁ
phrases.phonetic_text: tho skwu ohsta nitsatvnhe
phrases.phonetic_broad: to skwu osta nitsatvne
phrases.english_text: Y’all had it really good there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏃᎦᏛᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: ika ohsta nokatvnv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ika osta nokatvnv
phrases.english_text: We did really well.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏴᏣᏚᎳᎨ ᏫᎦᏤᏓᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᏣᏛᏒ
phrases.phonetic_text: yvtsatulakhe wi'katsetahsti yiki ski tsinuhst tsatvhsv
phrases.phonetic_broad: yvtsatulake wikatsetasti yiki ski tsinust tsatvsv
phrases.english_text: Would you want to go back there, to the way it was when you grew up?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎲ ᎥᎲ ᎬᏇᏓᏍᏗ ᎠᎹᏰ ᏱᎩ ᎠᎮ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏳᏫᎨᏓ Ꮎ ᏥᏳ ᎩᎶ ᎬᏆᏘᏃᎯᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ ᎥᎿᎮᏃ Ᏼ ᏭᎵᏍᏙ ᏴᏓᎭ ᎠᎹᏱ ᏭᏏᏅᏌ
phrases.phonetic_text: awtulhv vhv kvkwetahsti amay yki ahe eliwu yuwiket na tsiyu khilo kkwathinhohihsti yiki vnhheno yv wulhsto yvtaha amay wuhsinvhsa
phrases.phonetic_broad: awtulv vv kvkwetasti amay yki ae eliwu yuwiket na tsiyu kilo kkwatinoisti yiki vneno yv wulsto yvtaa amay wusinvsa
phrases.english_text: Uh-huh, I do want to go back there. I could go to the water if someone would bring me in a boat, because sometimes the water edge would be right there when the water receded.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎯᎢᏛ ᏱᏣᏛᏁᏗ ᏦᎮᎮᎢᏍ ᏣᏥ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsatelhokwa'v tsatahstayvhti hi'itv yitsatvnt tsohehe'ihs tsatsi
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsatelokwav tsatastayvti iitv yitsatvnt tsoeeis tsatsi
phrases.english_text: When you learned to cook, did your mom tell you, “This is how to cook”? Or did you just watch her?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᎪᎨ ᎯᎦᏙᏍᏛᏭ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsikokhe hikathohstvwu
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsikoke ikatostvwu
phrases.english_text: When you learned to cook, did your mom tell you, “This is how to cook”? Or did you just watch her?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᎦᏙᏍᏛᏊ ᏥᏛᏆᎴᏅᎲ ᏃᏭᏃ ᏢᏴ ᏃᏭ ᏣᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗᏛ ᏃᏭ ᎥᏉᎮᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsikathohstvkwu tsitvkwlenhv nowuno lhvyv nowu tsatelhohkwahsttv nowu vkwohehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsikatostvkwu tsitvkwlenv nowuno lvyv nowu tsatelokwasttv nowu vkwoev
phrases.english_text: When I started, I just watched her. Then a little later on I was told, "You have to learn,” then I learned. And also Grandma taught me how the elders cook things. What do they call them? They call them diguhe, cornbread. She used to make them about this [gestures] size.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᏆᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏃᏭ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᎴᏍᏊ ᏣᏪᏲᎲᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵ ᎤᏅᏂᏍᏙᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏙᏗ ᏓᏃᏎᎰ ᏗᎫᎮ ᏥᏕᎪᎮᎲ Ꮎ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsakwatelhohkwa'v nowu elhsi tsikehv nowulhskwu tsawyhohvhskv na anikayvli unvnhihstoti khuhst toti tanohseho tikuhe tsitekohehv na
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsakwatelokwav nowu elsi tsikev nowulskwu tsawyovskv na anikayvli unvnistoti kust toti tanoseo tikue tsitekoev na
phrases.english_text: When I started, I just watched her. Then a little later on I was told, "You have to learn,” then I learned. And also Grandma taught me how the elders cook things. What do they call them? They call them diguhe, cornbread. She used to make them about this [gestures] size.

phrases.syllabary_text: Corn Bread ᎯᎢᏴ ᎢᏗᎩᏓ ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: khawn twat hi'iyv itikit tsitektlhskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: kawn twat iiyv itikit tsitektlskv
phrases.english_text: When I started, I just watched her. Then a little later on I was told, "You have to learn,” then I learned. And also Grandma taught me how the elders cook things. What do they call them? They call them diguhe, cornbread. She used to make them about this [gestures] size.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏂᏐᏩᎸᏍ
phrases.phonetic_text: anihsowalhs
phrases.phonetic_broad: anisowals
phrases.english_text: Are they round?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏂᏐᏩᎸ dog headsᎮ ᏓᏃᏎᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: anihsowalv tak hathshe tanhsehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: anisowalv tak atse tansev
phrases.english_text: The round ones they called dog heads.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏛ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v akilvkwotv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv akilvkwotv
phrases.english_text: Yes, I really liked them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᎾᏅ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᏉᏢᏗ ᏣᏇᏲᏅ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏚᏯ ᎠᏑᏱ ᎦᏚ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏣᏪᏲᏅ ᎤᏖᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: skinanv iyuhst tikwolhvhti tsakwehyon nowule thuya ahsuyi katu nowule tsaweyonv utheti
phrases.phonetic_broad: skinanv iyust tikwolvti tsakweyon nowule tuya asuyi katu nowule tsaweyonv uteti
phrases.english_text: She taught me how to make that kind, and she also taught me bean bread. Delicious!

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᏛ ᏥᏕᎯᏃᎮ dog heads ᎤᏗᏞᎩ ᎪᎢ ᎠᎻᏃ ᎠᏑᏴ
phrases.phonetic_text: nat tshithinohe tak haths utilhek ko'i amino ahsuyv
phrases.phonetic_broad: nat tsitinoe tak ats utilek koi amino asuyv
phrases.english_text: The dog heads you're talking about, hot grease and salt was mixed in.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏳ ᎤᏖᏗ bacon grease ᎠᏑᏴᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: toyu uththi tekhan kwihs ahsuynv
phrases.phonetic_broad: toyu utti tekan kwis asuynv
phrases.english_text: It’s really delicious, with bacon grease mixed in.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏧᏍᏆᎸᏕ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsuhskwalte
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsuskwalte
phrases.english_text: Sure is that way.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᏍᎩᏃ ᏍᏊ ᎣᎬᏌᎮᏃ ᏦᏦᏢᏍᎬ Ꮎ butter ᏙᏳ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏖᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎦᏅᎵᏰᏗ Ꮎ dog heads
phrases.phonetic_text: vhskin skwu okvhsheno tsotsolhvhskv na tata toyhu skwu utheti skin tikanvliyti na tak haths
phrases.phonetic_broad: vskin skwu okvseno tsotsolvskv na tata toyu skwu uteti skin tikanvliyti na tak ats
phrases.english_text: We also made our own butter. It was also really delicious to spread on them, the dog heads.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ Ꮭ Ᏺ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎬᏁᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: o la yo ihlhvhiyu ski yikvnelv
phrases.phonetic_broad: o la yo ilviyu ski yikvnelv
phrases.english_text: I’ve never tried it that way.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏳ ᎤᏖᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎪᏢᏅ butter ᎤᏅᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ
phrases.phonetic_text: tyu utheht ski skwu uwhahs kolhvnhv tata unvtinv skwu
phrases.phonetic_broad: tyu utet ski skwu uwas kolvnv tata unvtinv skwu
phrases.english_text: It’s really delicious, just with butter and also cream.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᎾ ᎤᎦᏗᏢᏓ creamᎢᏍ ᏣᏃᏢᏍᎪ
phrases.phonetic_text: nana ukhatilhvta khwimhihs tsanolhvhsko
phrases.phonetic_broad: nana ukatilvta kwimis tsanolvsko
phrases.english_text: What about what they call cream? Did you all milk the cows?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᏊᏅ ᏕᏥᏁᎩᎡᎮ ᏩᎦ
phrases.phonetic_text: skwunv tetsineki'ehe waka
phrases.phonetic_broad: skwunv tetsinekiee waka
phrases.english_text: What about what they call cream? Did you all milk the cows?

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭵ ᏙᏥᏁᎩᎡᎲ ᏍᎩᏅ cream ᏍᏊ ᏥᎦᎾᏕᎬᎮᏅ cream butterᎢᏃ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎦᎾᏕᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: v ttsineki'ehv skihnv khwim skwu tsikanatekvhenv khwim tata'ino skwu tsikanatekv
phrases.phonetic_broad: v ttsinekiev skinv kwim skwu tsikanatekvenv kwim tataino skwu tsikanatekv
phrases.english_text: Yes, we milked them. That cream too, she sold the cream and also butter.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᏗᎨᏣᏙ ᏗᏣᏓᎸᎴ ᏱᎩ ᏂᎦᏗᏍ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎢᏥᏬᏂᏍᎨ
phrases.phonetic_text: na tiketsa'to titsatalvle yiki nikathihs tsalaki itsiwonhihske
phrases.phonetic_broad: na tiketsato titsatalvle yiki nikatis tsalaki itsiwoniske
phrases.english_text: Your brothers or sisters, did you all speak Cherokee?

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎦᏬᏂ ᎾᏍᏊ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᏥᏬᏂ ᏣᎳᎩ
phrases.phonetic_text: na vkito kawoni nahskwu tsohsttalv nikata otsiwoni tsalaki
phrases.phonetic_broad: na vkito kawoni naskwu tsosttalv nikata otsiwoni tsalaki
phrases.english_text: My brother speaks and so does my sister. We all speak Cherokee.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏏᏍ ᏕᏣᏓᏩᏛᎯᏙᎰ
phrases.phonetic_text: sihs tetsatawhahthitoho
phrases.phonetic_broad: sis tetsatawatitoo
phrases.english_text: Do you all still visit one another?

phrases.english_text: Yes, I only knew my grandmother, my mom’s mom, and her grandma had come on the Trail of Tears. She came when she was a little girl. What she was told, Grandma told me about it. It was really bad for them, the way the Indians were treated, she told me when she [Great Grandma] was a little girl coming on that trail.

phrases.phonetic_broad: ikttv ikatnve unvs kee yunnikisa nanv tlv aninae ae
phrases.english_text: Some, maybe some of them left by themselves. They might have been laying down somewhere.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᏝᏪ ᏄᎾᏛᏁ ᏝᎮᏃ ᏳᏓᎷᎳ ᏩᏯ ᎠᏎ ᎬᏩᏯᎡ ᏴᏓ ᎠᏎ ᎨᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: elawe nunatvne lheno yutalula waya ahse kvwayha'e yvta ahse khe
phrases.phonetic_broad: elawe nunatvne leno yutalula waya ase kvwayae yvta ase ke
phrases.english_text: They were quiet. It might be said that wolves must have not waited long to eat them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏧᎾᎵᎪᏔᏃᏅᎮ ᏱᎩ ᏧᎪᎳ ᏕᏥᏰ ᎥᎿ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ ᏍᏊ ᏴᏓᎭ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏣᎾᎵᏍᎦᏃᎲᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎬᎿᎨ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsunalikhothanonhe yhiki tsukhola tetsiye vnh ski ikatanvthehsko skwu yvtaha nikat tsanalhskanhvhskv na anikvnhake
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsunalikotanone yiki tsukola tetsiye vn ski ikatanvtesko skwu yvtaa nikat tsanalskanvskv na anikvnake
phrases.english_text: Scattered the bones and things. That’s what I think about sometimes, all these protests that they do, black people. They haven’t really had it all that bad, wanting to be helped because they’ve been treated so bad, they say. They weren’t treated as bad as the Indians.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏝᏙᎧ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎦ ᎤᏲ ᏍᎩᎢᎦ ᎤᏲ ᏳᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎴ ᏱᎩ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏣᎾᏓᎾᏟᏍᎪ ᎤᏲ ᎨᎩᎬᏁᎵ ᏣᎾᏗᎰ ᏝᏃ ᎠᏂᏴᏫᏯ ᏱᏄᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎴ ᏳᏲ ᏱᎨᎬᏁᎴ ᏱᎩ
phrases.phonetic_text: tlatokh ski yika uyo ski'ika uy yunalhstanhele yki nikata tsanhatanhatlihsko uyo kekkvneli tsanatiho tlhano aniyvwiy yinunalhstanele yuyo yikekvnel yiki
phrases.phonetic_broad: tlatok ski yika uyo skiika uy yunalstanele yki nikata tsanatanatlisko uyo kekkvneli tsanatio tlano aniyvwiy yinunalstanele yuyo yikekvnel yiki
phrases.english_text: Scattered the bones and things. That’s what I think about sometimes, all these protests that they do, black people. They haven’t really had it all that bad, wanting to be helped because they’ve been treated so bad, they say. They weren’t treated as bad as the Indians.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎦᏓ ᎾᏅ Ꮎ
phrases.phonetic_text: nika'ta nnv na
phrases.phonetic_broad: nikata nnv na
phrases.english_text: Everything and also… As you said, “We were chased off,” that’s what happened to them isn’t it?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᎩᎨᎯᏙᎴ ᏣᏗ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏥᏂᎨᎬᏁᎴ ᏓᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: tokkhehitol tsat skitv tsinikekvnel taha
phrases.phonetic_broad: tokkeitol tsat skitv tsinikekvnel taa
phrases.english_text: Everything and also… As you said, “We were chased off,” that’s what happened to them isn’t it?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᏍᎩ ᏂᎨᎬᏁᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: vhski nikekvnele
phrases.phonetic_broad: vski nikekvnele
phrases.english_text: That's what was done to them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎦᏓ ᎦᏓ ᏚᏂᎿᎡ ᏚᏂᏲᎱᏎᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: nikat kat tuninha'e tuniyohuhsele
phrases.phonetic_broad: nikat kat tuninae tuniyousele
phrases.english_text: They lost all the land they had.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ ᎨᏥᎩᎣᏁᎴ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏢᏃ ᏕᎨᏥᏍᏚᏅ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᎨᏥᏟᏏᏍᎨ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ Ꮎ
phrases.phonetic_text: aniyohsk ketsiki'onhele kohuhst tlvno teketsihstunhv anatiho ketsitlhihsihske ikohita na
phrases.phonetic_broad: aniyosk ketsikionele koust tlvno teketsistunv anatio ketsitlisiske ikoita na
phrases.english_text: The soldiers took everything from them. Somewhere they were locked up, they say, gathering them all together for that forced march. A lot of them died while they were rounded up.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏅᏓᎨᎨᏥᎢᎸᏍᏗ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏍᏊ ᏚᏂᏲᎱᏒ ᎠᎾᏗᎲᏅ ᎨᏥᏍᏚᏅ ᏓᏂᏟᏏᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: ntakketsi'ilvhsti tskwihsti skwu tuniyohuhsv anatihvnhv ketsihstunv tanilhihsihskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ntakketsiilvsti tskwisti skwu tuniyousv anativnv ketsistunv tanilisiskv
phrases.english_text: The soldiers took everything from them. Somewhere they were locked up, they say, gathering them all together for that forced march. A lot of them died while they were rounded up.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏝᎮᏃ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᎬᎾᏈᏴᎰ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᏲ ᏂᏚᏅᏁᎴ ᏂᎨᎬᏁᎴ ᎠᏯᎮᏃ ᏂᎨᎬᏁᎴ ᏍᏊ ᏁᎳᎩ ᏂᎩᎦᏛᎴᏒᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: lheno ilvhiy yikvnakwhiyvho nuhstv uyo nitunvnelhe nikekvnele ayhen nikkvnele skwu nelaki nikikathvlehsvna tsikehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: leno ilviy yikvnakwiyvo nustv uyo nitunvnele nikekvnele ayen nikkvnele skwu nelaki nikikatvlesvna tsikev
phrases.english_text: They have never paid for it, what harm they caused them. What was done to them was done to us also, even though we didn’t go through it.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎢᎩᏠᏱ ᏥᏄᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏯᏍᎩᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏅᏓᏳᏂᎩᏓ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎤᎵᏏ ᎨᎲ ᎹᎹᎢᏃ ᎠᏯᏃ ᏦᎢᏁᏭᏃ ᎢᏴ
phrases.phonetic_text: ikilhoy tsinnalihstanelv ayahskinv na akeyhuhtsa nvtayunhikitha elihs nowu tsikehv akvyi ulihs kehv mam'ino ayano tso'inewhuno iyv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ikiloy tsinnalistanelv ayaskinv na akeyutsa nvtayunikita elis nowu tsikev akvyi ulis kev mamino ayano tsoinewuno iyv
phrases.english_text: It happened to our families. But us, she came when she was a girl, it was Grandma’s Grandma. And Mama and my third grandma who came as a little girl.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵᏏ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᏓᏳᎶᏒ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ
phrases.phonetic_text: elihs kehv skina na tayulohsv na uhsti akeyhutsa
phrases.phonetic_broad: elis kev skina na tayulosv na usti akeyutsa
phrases.english_text: It happened to our families. But us, she came when she was a girl, it was Grandma’s Grandma. And Mama and my third grandma who came as a little girl.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏳᎭ ᎤᏲ ᎤᎪᎲᏁ ᏙᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: toyuha uyo ukohvne toha
phrases.phonetic_broad: toyua uyo ukovne toa
phrases.english_text: She really saw some bad things, didn't she?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᎪᎲᏁ ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: ukohvne v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: ukovne vv
phrases.english_text: Yes, she saw different things.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎩᎶ Ꮭ ᏳᏚᎵ ᎤᎪᏩᏛᏗ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᎤᎪᎲᏁ ᎨᏒ
phrases.phonetic_text: khilo la yutuli ukowahtthi iyuhsti ukohvne kehsv
phrases.phonetic_broad: kilo la yutuli ukowatti iyusti ukovne kesv
phrases.english_text: Someone wouldn’t want to see all the things she saw.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᏲᎢᏃ ᏄᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎤᏬᏚᎯᏃ ᎨᎲᎧ ᏍᏊ ᏧᎾᏂᎩᏎ
phrases.phonetic_text: uyo'in nunalhstanhelv uwotuhino khehvkh skwu tsunanhikihse
phrases.phonetic_broad: uyoin nunalstanelv uwotuino kevk skwu tsunanikise
phrases.english_text: It was hard for them. Isn’t it beautiful, where they came from?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᏬᏚ ᏙᎡ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᎾᏛᏅ ᏧᎾᏂᎩᏎ
phrases.phonetic_text: uwot'u to'e ohsta nunatvnv tsunanikihse
phrases.phonetic_broad: uwotu toe osta nunatvnv tsunanikise

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᎾᏛᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: ohsta nunatvnhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: osta nunatvnv
phrases.english_text: They were doing well.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᎮᏃ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎦᏓᏅᏖᎭ ᏫᏥᏯᏘᏂᏓᏍᏗ Georgia Ꮎ Vann Mansion ᏣᏂᏃᎮᏍᎪ
phrases.phonetic_text: naheno akhstayvhvhsk katanvthha witsiyathinitahsti tsawtsa na tan manhsan tsaninhehsko
phrases.phonetic_broad: naeno akstayvvsk katanvta witsiyatinitasti tsawtsa na tan mansan tsaninesko
phrases.english_text: My wife, I’m thinking about taking her there to Georgia. Vann Mansion, they talk about, Vann was my wife’s last name. Jim Vann owned Vann Mansion. Somewhere there they were left behind they say, her relatives. I don’t know for sure; I just want to take her there.

phrases.syllabary_text: VannᎮᏃ ᏭᏛ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Vann Mansion ᎤᏬᏢᎯ Jim Vann ᏚᏙᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎩᏅᏍ
phrases.phonetic_text: tanhen wutv akhstayvhvhsk skinana tan manhsan uwolhi tsim tan tuto'v skina skinvhs
phrases.phonetic_broad: tanen wutv akstayvvsk skinana tan mansan uwoli tsim tan tutov skina skinvs
phrases.english_text: My wife, I’m thinking about taking her there to Georgia. Vann Mansion, they talk about, Vann was my wife’s last name. Jim Vann owned Vann Mansion. Somewhere there they were left behind they say, her relatives. I don’t know for sure; I just want to take her there.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮲ ᎨᏒ ᎤᎾᏓᏂᏴᏓ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᏝᏃ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ Ꮩ ᏱᎩ ᎠᏎᏅ ᎠᏆᏚᎵᏭ ᏫᏥᏯᏘᏂᏓᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: lhv kehsv unta'niyhvhta anhahtiho tlano yawanvth to yiki ahsenhv akwatuliw witsiyathinitahsti
phrases.phonetic_broad: lv kesv untaniyvta anatio tlano yawanvt to yiki asenv akwatuliw witsiyatinitasti
phrases.english_text: My wife, I’m thinking about taking her there to Georgia. Vann Mansion, they talk about, Vann was my wife’s last name. Jim Vann owned Vann Mansion. Somewhere there they were left behind they say, her relatives. I don’t know for sure; I just want to take her there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵᏛ ᏱᏛᏩᏔ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏧᏩᏂ ᎬᎿ ᏚᎾᏂᎩᏒ
phrases.phonetic_text: elitv yitvwhath kohuhst tsuwanhi khvnha tunnikihsv
phrases.phonetic_broad: elitv yitvwat koust tsuwani kvna tunnikisv
phrases.english_text: You might be able to find some of her relatives there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎪᏪᎵᏴ ᏯᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎳ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏱᏛᏩᏔ
phrases.phonetic_text: kowheliy yahstawatitola eliwu yitvwhatha
phrases.phonetic_broad: koweliy yastawatitola eliwu yitvwata
phrases.english_text: If you follow the written records, you can find them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᎮᏃ Ꮎ last name ᎨᎲ ᎠᏂSwimmerᎮᏃ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏂᎷᏥᏝ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎯᎠ ᎢᏳᎾᏍᏗ Ꮭ Ꮟ ᏱᏗᏁᎮ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏱᎦᏓ ᏧᎾᏙᎢᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: ayahen na wahst nem khv anihswimmehen kehv uniluhtsilha skina hi'a iyunahst tlha si yitinehe eliwu yikat tsunto'ita
phrases.phonetic_broad: ayaen na wast nem kv aniswimmeen kev unilutsila skina ia iyunast tla si yitinee eliwu yikat tsuntoita
phrases.english_text: For me, our last name was Swimmer, when they got here. The ones with this name weren’t still living there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᏛ Ᏺ ᎠᏆᏅᏔ Ᏺ Ꮎ North Carolina ᎨᎲ Perry Shell ᏚᏙᎠ ᏤᎭ Ᏺ ᎣᎦᏅᏔ Ᏺ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏦᎬᏂ
phrases.phonetic_text: ayat yo akwanvtha yo nha nawt khawawana kehv thawi hsaw tuto'a tseha yo okanvtha yo kohuhst tsokvni
phrases.phonetic_broad: ayat yo akwanvta yo na nawt kawawana kev tawi saw tutoa tsea yo okanvta yo koust tsokvni
phrases.english_text: For me, I know in North Carolina, Perry Shell his name. We know we’re family.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᏖᏗ ᏱᎩ ᎬᏕᎶᎰᎯᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ ᎨᎵᎰ
phrases.phonetic_text: uthti yik kvtelhohihsti yik keliho
phrases.phonetic_broad: utti yik kvteloisti yik kelio
phrases.english_text: I think it’s really amazing to be able to find out.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᎳᏛᏴ ᏱᏛᏩᏔ ᏙᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: halatvyv ytvwhath tha
phrases.phonetic_broad: alatvyv ytvwat ta
phrases.english_text: You can find out a lot, ain’t it?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏱᏛᏩᏔ ᏥᏈᏍᏗᎡ ᏗᏁᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: tskwihst yithvwatha tsikw'ihsti'e tineha
phrases.phonetic_broad: tskwist yitvwata tsikwistie tinea
phrases.english_text: You can find a lot. There’s a lot living there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᏃ Marble City ᏣᏛᎦᏅ Ꮎ Marble City
phrases.phonetic_text: ayano mawtaw hsiti tstvkan na mawtaw hsiti
phrases.phonetic_broad: ayano mawtaw siti tstvkan na mawtaw siti
phrases.english_text: For me, Marble City, you’ve heard of Marble City? If somebody died over there, that’s your family, they’d say. I didn’t know anything about that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎦᏓᏲᏍᏗ ᎩᎶᏕ ᏱᏧᏲᎱᏌ ᎥᎿ ᎫᏍᏕᏍ ᏱᎬᏁᏗ ᏯᎾᏓ ᎾᏆᏅᏛᏂ ᎨᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: katayohsti khilote yitsuyohuhsa vnha kuhstehs yikvnheti yanata nakwanvtni kehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: katayosti kilote yitsuyousa vna kustes yikvneti yanata nakwanvtni kev
phrases.english_text: For me, Marble City, you’ve heard of Marble City? If somebody died over there, that’s your family, they’d say. I didn’t know anything about that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᏃ ᏂᎦᏥᏪᎮᎸ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᏓᎾᏛᏍᎬ ᎥᎿ Dry Creek ᎮᏍᏗ ᏱᏗᏣᎦᏎᏍᏗᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ ᎥᎿ ᏗᏁᎲ ᏂᎦᏗᏍ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏗᏨᏂ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎣᏏᏃ ᎤᏃᎯᏳᏁ Ꮩ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᎾᏛᏁᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: skino nikatsiwhelv anitshuths tanthskv vnha twa khwikh hehsti yittsakahsehstihehsti anikeyutsa vnh tinehv nikatihs kohuhst ttsvni kahtsyohehv ohsino unohiyune to lha ski yinunatvnele
phrases.phonetic_broad: skino nikatsiwelv anitsuts tantskv vna twa kwik esti yittsakasestiesti anikeyutsa vn tinev nikatis koust ttsvni katsyoev osino unoiyune to la ski yinunatvnele
phrases.english_text: That’s what I told my boys growing up in Dry Creek. “Don’t look for girls over there, you’re related to everybody”. They really believed it; they didn’t do that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᏛ Ꮎ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᏣᏛᎦᏅᏅᎮ ᏍᏊ Greasy ᏣᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: aytv na akhstayhvhski tstvkanvnvhe skwu kwihsi tsaninhehskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: aytv na akstayvski tstvkanvnve skwu kwisi tsanineskv
phrases.english_text: As for me, my wife, you’ve heard of Greasy, that they were talking about? There on the other side, used to be what they call Kentucky. If we talk about things like that, I will say we’re not related, I married her from Kentucky, my wife I told them… Let’s talk about how you all grew up. We killed hogs, you said. Were you able to help, were you old enough to help?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎿᏭ ᎠᏗᏜᏴ Kentucky
phrases.phonetic_text: vnhawu atilyv khantakhi
phrases.phonetic_broad: vnawu atilyv kantaki
phrases.english_text: As for me, my wife, you’ve heard of Greasy, that they were talking about? There on the other side, used to be what they call Kentucky. If we talk about things like that, I will say we’re not related, I married her from Kentucky, my wife I told them… Let’s talk about how you all grew up. We killed hogs, you said. Were you able to help, were you old enough to help?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏃᎮᎭᎮᏃ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏃ ᏲᎩᏃᎮᏝ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎠᏋᏂ ᏱᎩ Kentucky ᏫᏥᏯᏅᎲ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: anohehahen tsikehv skin yokinohela tlha kohuhsti akwvni yik khantakhi witsiyanhv akhihstayhvhski katsiyohehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: anoeaen tsikev skin yokinoela tla kousti akwvni yik kantaki witsiyanv akistayvski katsiyoev
phrases.english_text: As for me, my wife, you’ve heard of Greasy, that they were talking about? There on the other side, used to be what they call Kentucky. If we talk about things like that, I will say we’re not related, I married her from Kentucky, my wife I told them… Let’s talk about how you all grew up. We killed hogs, you said. phrases.phonetic_broad: e yikanvto iyusti ekinev

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᎾᏅᏛᎡ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᎢᎾᏓ ᎤᎦᎹ ᏯᏅᏗᎮ ᏱᎨᎵ

phrases.english_text: Just Cherokee.

phrases.english_text: It took me quite a while and I say I'm still learning it today.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᏢᏃ ᏕᏣᏕᎶᏆᎡ
phrases.phonetic_text: halhvno tetsatelhokwa'e
phrases.phonetic_broad: alvno tetsatelokwae

phrases.english_text: Yeah.

I finished at Bacone, but something happened towards the end, and I failed the exam and I didn’t go back a second time. Yeah, I went back and all I had left to finish were some classes. I think I really made a mistake.

phrases.english_text: But I went back and started working at City Hospital. Nineteen years I worked there. They were paying more when I finished school, but I didn’t get my license.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᎪᏛ Ᏺ ᎬᏩᏈᏴᎡᎲ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎩᏍᏆᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏝᏃ license ᏯᎩᏁᏎ

phrases.phonetic_broad: asenv tsalvkwoteno skwu elist ta
phrases.english_text: But it seems like you liked it, right?

phrases.english_text: How come your eyes are getting weak, is there not anything they can do to them to see a little better?

phrases.english_text: They are trying. I go to Tulsa, and I go here in town. When it gets worse, I go to Tulsa, when they can’t help me here. It started as glaucoma. They didn’t know what it was here at first, when it started. Something happened inside and they couldn’t fix it. One time we went to Crosslin, a healer that lived in Sallisaw. And he took me to water. Really a wonder what happened then, the way my eyes are now, I can’t see anything. It’s just white is all I see in here. I can’t see you two. That’s the way they were when we got there. He told me what I needed was to go to water, so that’s what he did, he took me to water. And when my husband and I left, as we got on the road and past the stomp grounds, my eye started itching. So, I closed my eyes and rubbed my eye, and when I opened them, I could see, just that quick it was good, he healed me. He was a real good healer; I was able to see for a long time after that. My husband, something happened to his heart then at the time. I was sitting up too much at night, I couldn’t sleep; that’s when it started. My eyesight got weak or fading, but not all of it faded out. I could still see a bit. Then five years ago, suddenly I lost my eyesight, but I still have hope.

phrases.english_text: That’s how it was sometimes when people were around, they would tell stories. What happened in the past, and then at night she started telling me things until I was asleep. She talked about a lot of things that her grandma had told her. Where we were, they talked a little bit about what they call Juhlgal. It’s something tall. How Grandma described it to me was a little different, but there was one thing she used to talk about. There was a tree, and the women, there were these beans that grew back then, they would go up the mountain looking for where those beans grew, to cook them. About halfway up, they were sitting down when something started making a sound. When they looked up there, there was something standing between the tree branches. The girl said there was something tall in between the branches, it looked like a star she said, Grandma said. When we were there in the valley where they had been, I didn’t go. It was too rough for me to go, I was told. They were saying there were markings, something that Juhlgal had done. They said those markings, no one can read what it’s saying. They said when they went, some of them went to look at it. They say that Juhlgal had done that, they were saying.

phrases.english_text: Yes, she told me a lot of things. And the Indians that were there, they danced, and one time they were saying if a panther was coming it would howl. If a panther was coming, they would stay behind to build fires at the dance ground, because the panther was afraid of fire. One time they left behind a blind old woman, she was staying at their home. She could hear the panther growling as it was coming near. The old woman didn’t know what she was going to do. “When it finds out I am in here, it will come eat me,” the old woman thought. So, she heated up some water, bringing it to a boil. Sure enough, the panther came in. The houses that they lived in were like tents covered in tree leaves, and when it opened the woman sat there, and did this [gestures] to the panther. When it opened, the panther was splashed with hot water, and it ran off, backing away because it had been scalded. The next morning, the dancers returned, and the panther wasn’t there. It was hurt too badly, and so the dancers had to go kill it.

phrases.english_text: She taught me a little bit, but it was too long, I couldn’t learn all of it. But it was good to learn in someone was chasing us, she would say. That’s the kind of strong medicine he used to go around using. That’s why he avoided them for so long, she used to say.

phrases.english_text: They were bad. One time she said, “This man’s wife was running around on him. So, she went to a dance and left the boy to stay with his grandma.” I think they were staying with her. “Let her go,” Grandma told the boy when the wife left. She didn’t take much of her things. The old woman sat in front of the fireplace and put all she had down. And there, the boy saw she had laid out some arrowheads. She had hung what they call a moccasin––you know the kind made out of deer skin––she hung it in front of where she had the arrowheads. Later on, she left and one of the arrowheads made a sound, so she went to where the bundle was on the chimney. Later on, when she came back, she said to the flint, “You didn’t do anything.” So then she sent another arrowhead and again when it came back it hadn’t done anything. “You didn’t go do anything either,” she said to it. Then she put it away. When the third one left and came back she had a container this [gestures] size with water, and the arrowhead went into it. It was washed, and the arrowhead had blood on it. “You really did something,” she said to it, then she put it up. Later on, someone came and told the boy that his wife had died at the dance. The flint must have shot her.

phrases.phonetic_broad: siwuts soi
phrases.english_text: Another one? Let's see… because there’s a lot of things I know. Also, the Ukten that they talk about, have you all heard of it? One time she said they went fishing. Standing Rock, as they call it, by Oklahoma Station, near where the river is. Standing Rock, as they called it, because Grandma said a rock used to stand there. It’s underwater. These days the water isn’t as deep as she was saying around that area. There, a tree that had fallen was there. Grandma would sit on it before others started coming to fish there in the deep end. Long dresses, they wore back then. Her dress was in the way of her fishing. After a while something was moving below, she saw it and looked. It looked like a cow. It was looking at her from below. It was kind of like a greenish color, she said. Its eyes were like a cow, and its nose too, and it had horns. She watched it, she thought, “What am I going to do?” The others fishing there, she didn’t want to yell at them. “Let’s get down for a little while,” she told them, walking away. “Let’s get down for a while”. They all started walking back. They didn’t ask why when they were told to get off. When they went up a little further, she told them, and that’s when they started running, she said. That was Ukten, she used to say. That’s where it lives, she used to say, in the deep end of the water, there near Standing Rock. I think there are still some things that are living in the deep end of the water.

That girl too, she started jumping around. “Come back!” Then the boy started to run back. All of a sudden, it came up, that thing like a snake. phrases.english_text: Yes, those too. She told one about when they were taking care of a sick person, the medicine man was doctoring them and couldn’t cure them. Then someone checked. A raven is disturbing this one. They can’t get better unless it takes them, she was told. Unless you get somebody brave and young. You get them, tonight this doorway on both sides they will sit, because the raven will come back, they were told. There were two brave young men. “We will do it!” they said. They used medicine on them and were seated next to the doorway. Back then when somebody was sick, people would come, they would be outside and have a fire going, that’s how they were. The young men that were treated with medicine heard something in the distance. They had been told what was going to happen. They were waiting on it. The second time they heard the noise it was a little closer, and a third, and a fourth, and then on the steps landed a beautiful woman. She wore a long knife on her side, as she walked, she didn’t see the boys watching over the sick person. When the woman got to the doorway, the boys grabbed her. She was very strong, I think. She almost got away from the young boys. She was slinging them around, but they held on to her until morning came. That morning, when it got light out, they let her go. The woman was naked. The dress she had was covered in corn and it broke and left her naked. I don’t know if she lived close by or not. Nobody heard anything about anyone passing away, because she was going to die when she got home, they were told. But they didn’t hear anything. I guess she must’ve lived too far away. Then the sick person began to get better. That’s what was coming to the sickly person, that raven demon.

phrases.english_text: Yes, those too. She told one about when they were taking care of a sick person, the medicine man was doctoring them and couldn’t cure them. Then someone checked. A raven is disturbing this one. They can’t get better unless it takes them, she was told. Unless you get somebody brave and young. You get them, tonight this doorway on both sides they will sit, because the raven will come back, they were told. There were two brave young men. “We will do it!” they said. They used medicine on them and were seated next to the doorway. Back then when somebody was sick, people would come, they would be outside and have a fire going, that’s how they were. The young men that were treated with medicine heard something in the distance. They had been told what was going to happen. They were waiting on it. The second time they heard the noise it was a little closer, and a third, and a fourth, and then on the steps landed a beautiful woman. She wore a long knife on her side, as she walked, she didn’t see the boys watching over the sick person. When the woman got to the doorway, the boys grabbed her. She was very strong, I think. She almost got away from the young boys. She was slinging them around, but they held on to her until morning came. That morning, when it got light out, they let her go. The woman was naked. The dress she had was covered in corn and it broke and left her naked. I don’t know if she lived close by or not. Nobody heard anything about anyone passing away, because she was going to die when she got home, they were told. But they didn’t hear anything. I guess she must’ve lived too far away. Then the sick person began to get better. That’s what was coming to the sickly person, that raven demon.

phrases.english_text: Yes, those too. She told one about when they were taking care of a sick person, the medicine man was doctoring them and couldn’t cure them. Then someone checked. A raven is disturbing this one. They can’t get better unless it takes them, she was told. Unless you get somebody brave and young. You get them, tonight this doorway on both sides they will sit, because the raven will come back, they were told. There were two brave young men. “We will do it!” they said. They used medicine on them and were seated next to the doorway. Back then when somebody was sick, people would come, they would be outside and have a fire going, that’s how they were. The young men that were treated with medicine heard something in the distance. They had been told what was going to happen. They were waiting on it. The second time they heard the noise it was a little closer, and a third, and a fourth, and then on the steps landed a beautiful woman. She wore a long knife on her side, as she walked, she didn’t see the boys watching over the sick person. When the woman got to the doorway, the boys grabbed her. She was very strong, I think. She almost got away from the young boys. She was slinging them around, but they held on to her until morning came. That morning, when it got light out, they let her go. The woman was naked. The dress she had was covered in corn and it broke and left her naked. I don’t know if she lived close by or not. Nobody heard anything about anyone passing away, because she was going to die when she got home, they were told. But they didn’t hear anything. I guess she must’ve lived too far away. Then the sick person began to get better. That’s what was coming to the sickly person, that raven demon.

phrases.english_text: My wife’s uncle did that too. He grabbed it and held it until morning. When the morning came it was saying, “Let me go, let me go!” Her uncle’s name was Jake. “Jake let me go!” it was saying. While he was holding on to it, it started changing into something scary. Later on, Jake said, “I was holding on to a big rattlesnake”. That’s what it was changing to, but I knew it wasn’t really a rattlesnake, it was just a shapeshifter that was trying to scare him.
